description.value: A multimodal MRI study comparing structural and resting-state functional brain characteristics among first-episode drug-naive schizophrenia patients, medicated chronic schizophrenia patients, and normal controls, and using linear SVM with recursive feature elimination to classify the three groups.

spans.text: In this study, we recruited 44 first-episode drug-naive SZ (FESZ) patients, 44 medicated chronic SZ (CSZ) patients, and 56 normal controls (NCs) and acquired their structural and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

description.value: Cross-sectional observational comparison of three human cohorts: first-episode drug-naive schizophrenia, medicated chronic schizophrenia, and normal controls. Participants were recruited from Guangzhou Brain Hospital or the local community; no intervention assignment was reported.

spans.text: The FESZ, CSZ, and NC groups were recruited from Guangzhou Brain Hospital and the local community, respectively.

model_type.value: linear support vector machine with recursive feature elimination

spans.text: A linear support vector machine (SVM) combined with a recursive feature elimination (RFE) algorithm was implemented to discriminate three groups.

model_settings.value: Linear kernel; 10-fold cross-validation; recursive feature elimination ranked features by squared SVM weights; 1,000-label permutation test.

spans.text: A linear kernel SVM implemented in the Library for Support Vector Machines toolbox was used in this study.

value: tissue segmentation into GM, WM, and CSF

spans.text: First, each T1-weighted MRI was segmented into three tissue maps, including GM, WM, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by using the new segmentation algorithm from SPM8.
